questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What is an ERP system?
questions.preferred_answer: An enterprise resource planning system integrates core business processes and shared data across areas such as finance, procurement, inventory, manufacturing, projects, and human resources. Its value comes from common controls and a consistent transaction model, not merely from placing several modules under one login.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What is a CRM system?
questions.preferred_answer: A customer relationship management system supports the lifecycle of prospects and customers across sales, marketing, service, and related interactions. It should provide governed customer data, process visibility, activity history, and measurable outcomes rather than operate as a contact list alone.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What is meant by a business application?
questions.preferred_answer: A business application is software designed to execute, control, or analyze a business capability or process. It may be a packaged ERP or CRM module, an industry application, a low-code solution, or an extension connected to a wider enterprise platform.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: Why is a system of record important?
questions.preferred_answer: A system of record is the authoritative source for a defined data domain or transaction. Clear ownership prevents conflicting updates, simplifies reconciliation, and tells integrations which system may create or master each field.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: How does an integrated suite differ from a best-of-breed landscape?
questions.preferred_answer: An integrated suite usually offers a common data model, security model, and vendor roadmap, reducing some integration effort. Best-of-breed products can provide deeper capability in selected areas but require stronger architecture, identity, data governance, and support across vendors.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What is the difference between configuration and customization?
questions.preferred_answer: Configuration changes supported settings, metadata, workflows, or rules without altering the product core. Customization adds code or extensions for unmet requirements; it can be justified, but it raises testing, security, upgrade, and maintenance obligations.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: How do SaaS ERP and CRM differ operationally from on-premises products?
questions.preferred_answer: In SaaS, the vendor operates the underlying service and controls much of the upgrade cadence, while the customer remains responsible for data, access, configuration, integrations, testing, and adoption. On-premises deployments give more infrastructure control but require customer-managed availability, patching, capacity, and disaster recovery.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What does fit-to-standard mean?
questions.preferred_answer: Fit-to-standard starts with the product's standard process and asks the business to adopt it unless a requirement creates material legal, control, customer, or competitive value. Deviations should be documented with benefits, costs, risks, ownership, and lifecycle impact.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: Why should an ERP or CRM implementation begin with business value?
questions.preferred_answer: A value hypothesis connects the program to measurable outcomes such as faster close, improved forecast accuracy, lower order cycle time, better service resolution, or reduced control failures. Without it, teams can optimize features while failing to improve the business.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What is the difference between master data and transactional data?
questions.preferred_answer: Master data describes relatively stable business entities such as customers, products, suppliers, employees, and accounts. Transactional data records events such as orders, invoices, payments, cases, and inventory movements that reference those entities.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What does customer 360 mean in practice?
questions.preferred_answer: Customer 360 is a governed, role-appropriate view of customer identity, relationships, interactions, orders, service history, consent, and value. It does not require copying every field into one database; it requires consistent identity, ownership, access, and timely integration.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What are common ERP and CRM implementation roles?
questions.preferred_answer: Typical roles include executive sponsor, process owner, product owner, functional consultant, business analyst, solution architect, integration and data specialists, security lead, test lead, change lead, administrator, developer, and support owner. Clear decision rights matter more than job titles.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: How would you assess whether a requested feature belongs in ERP, CRM, or another application?
questions.preferred_answer: Evaluate process ownership, authoritative data, transaction boundaries, user population, latency, control requirements, reporting, and product capability. Place the capability where it has the cleanest ownership and lowest long-term integration and duplication cost.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: Why can a technically successful implementation still fail?
questions.preferred_answer: The system may be available and defect-free but still fail because processes are poorly designed, data is untrusted, users avoid it, controls are weak, benefits are not measured, or support cannot sustain it. Success must include business outcomes, adoption, control effectiveness, and operability.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: How should an organization govern overlapping capabilities across business applications?
questions.preferred_answer: Establish application and data ownership, architecture principles, a capability map, integration standards, and a decision forum. New requests should be evaluated for duplication, strategic fit, data authority, security, cost, and retirement impact.

questions.category: 1. ERP, CRM and Business Application Foundations
questions.question: What indicators would you use to evaluate an ERP or CRM program after go-live?
questions.preferred_answer: Use process cycle times, data quality, control exceptions, user adoption, transaction completion, service levels, integration reliability, defect trends, support volume, financial benefits, and stakeholder satisfaction. Compare results with the pre-implementation baseline and assigned benefit owners.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is an as-is process?
questions.preferred_answer: An as-is process documents how work is actually performed today, including systems, handoffs, controls, exceptions, data, delays, and unofficial workarounds. It creates a fact base for deciding what should be retained, simplified, automated, or stopped.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is a to-be process?
questions.preferred_answer: A to-be process defines the intended future way of working, including roles, decisions, controls, system interactions, measures, and exception handling. It should be feasible in the target operating model and traceable to business outcomes.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is a business requirement?
questions.preferred_answer: A business requirement states the outcome, capability, constraint, or rule the organization needs. It should describe the need before prescribing a specific screen, field, or technical implementation.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: Why use swimlanes in process mapping?
questions.preferred_answer: Swimlanes show responsibility across roles, teams, or systems and make handoffs visible. They help identify unclear ownership, duplicate approvals, manual re-entry, and control gaps.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is fit-gap analysis?
questions.preferred_answer: Fit-gap analysis compares business requirements with standard product capability. Each gap should be classified, prioritized, and resolved through process change, configuration, extension, integration, another application, or explicit rejection.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How do functional and nonfunctional requirements differ?
questions.preferred_answer: Functional requirements describe behavior and business rules; nonfunctional requirements describe qualities and constraints such as performance, availability, security, auditability, localization, accessibility, and supportability. Both must be testable.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How should acceptance criteria be written for a business application requirement?
questions.preferred_answer: Write observable conditions that define success, including role, trigger, data, expected result, permissions, errors, controls, and relevant performance limits. Avoid vague wording such as user-friendly or fast unless a measurable threshold is supplied.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is requirements traceability?
questions.preferred_answer: Traceability links business outcomes and requirements to design decisions, configurations, integrations, tests, training, and release artifacts. It helps control scope and proves that critical requirements and controls were validated.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How would you prioritize a backlog of ERP or CRM requirements?
questions.preferred_answer: Use business value, legal and control necessity, user impact, dependency, risk reduction, effort, and time criticality. A method such as MoSCoW can help, but decision owners and rationale must be recorded.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: Why must exception paths be captured during process discovery?
questions.preferred_answer: Standard happy paths often represent only part of operational workload. Returns, cancellations, partial deliveries, credit holds, duplicate customers, approval rejections, and integration failures drive complexity, controls, and support demand.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How do you identify business controls in a process workshop?
questions.preferred_answer: Ask where errors, fraud, unauthorized actions, or compliance failures could occur, then identify preventive and detective controls, evidence, owners, frequency, and escalation. Separate mandatory controls from historical approvals that add no value.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What is the purpose of a requirements prototype?
questions.preferred_answer: A prototype makes assumptions visible and lets users test navigation, data, rules, and terminology early. It is a learning tool, not proof that integration, security, performance, or full process behavior is complete.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How would you handle conflicting requirements from two business units?
questions.preferred_answer: Clarify the underlying outcome, legal context, data ownership, volume, and cost of variation. Seek a common standard with controlled exceptions; escalate unresolved policy decisions to the accountable process owner rather than letting configuration hide the conflict.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How can process mining support ERP transformation?
questions.preferred_answer: Process mining can reconstruct actual flows from event data to reveal variants, rework, delays, and conformance issues. It should complement interviews because logs may omit manual steps, business rationale, and data quality problems.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: How would you challenge a request to reproduce every legacy behavior?
questions.preferred_answer: Ask what outcome and risk the behavior addresses, whether the target product already provides a standard approach, and what the lifecycle cost of preserving it would be. Retain only behavior that is legally required or produces justified business value.

questions.category: 2. Business Process Discovery, Requirements and Fit-Gap Analysis
questions.question: What should a high-quality fit-gap decision record contain?
questions.preferred_answer: It should contain the requirement, process context, standard capability, gap description, options considered, selected disposition, value, risk, cost, dependencies, data and security impact, decision owner, date, and affected tests and training.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is a general ledger?
questions.preferred_answer: The general ledger is the primary accounting record where balanced journal entries are summarized by account, entity, period, and other dimensions. Subledgers such as receivables, payables, and assets normally post controlled entries into it.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is a chart of accounts?
questions.preferred_answer: A chart of accounts defines the account structure used to classify financial activity. A good design balances statutory and management reporting needs against excessive detail that complicates posting, reconciliation, and governance.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is procure-to-pay?
questions.preferred_answer: Procure-to-pay covers the flow from demand and supplier selection through requisition, purchase order, receipt, invoice validation, and payment. The system should preserve approvals, matching, liability recognition, and an auditable record.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is order-to-cash?
questions.preferred_answer: Order-to-cash covers customer order capture, pricing and credit checks, fulfillment, shipping or service delivery, invoicing, collection, and settlement. It crosses sales, logistics, finance, tax, and customer service.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is a subledger and why is it reconciled to the general ledger?
questions.preferred_answer: A subledger stores detailed transactions for a domain such as customers, suppliers, or assets. Reconciliation confirms that its control account balance agrees with the general ledger and identifies missing, duplicate, or misclassified postings.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: Explain two-way and three-way invoice matching.
questions.preferred_answer: Two-way matching compares invoice information with the purchase order. Three-way matching also includes the receipt or service confirmation, helping prevent payment for incorrect quantities, prices, or undelivered goods.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What controls would you expect around vendor creation and payment?
questions.preferred_answer: Separate vendor master maintenance from invoice entry and payment approval, validate bank changes, require evidence and approvals, screen duplicates, restrict privileged access, and monitor unusual payments. Emergency changes need documented review.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: How do credit limits affect order-to-cash?
questions.preferred_answer: Credit checks can warn, block, or route orders for approval when exposure exceeds policy. The design should define exposure calculation, exceptions, overrides, ownership, and how releases are audited.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is an accounting period close?
questions.preferred_answer: Period close is the controlled completion of accounting activities for a reporting period, including posting cutoffs, subledger processing, reconciliations, adjustments, consolidation, review, and locking. Dependencies and evidence should be managed through a close calendar.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: How should tax configuration be governed?
questions.preferred_answer: Tax rules should be owned by qualified finance or tax stakeholders, mapped to jurisdictions and transaction conditions, tested with representative scenarios, versioned, and monitored after regulatory change. Manual overrides should be restricted and reported.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What is intercompany processing?
questions.preferred_answer: Intercompany processing records transactions between entities in the same group and supports reciprocal postings, transfer pricing, settlement, and elimination. Master data and cutoffs must be consistent to avoid consolidation mismatches.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: How would you investigate an invoice that posted to the wrong expense account?
questions.preferred_answer: Trace account determination from supplier, item or category, purchase order, receipt, invoice, and configuration. Confirm whether the issue is master data, mapping, override, rule precedence, or user selection, then correct safely and test related scenarios.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: How would you design approval limits for purchases?
questions.preferred_answer: Base approval on risk-relevant dimensions such as amount, category, entity, budget, supplier, and exception type. Avoid unnecessary serial approvals; define delegation, escalation, conflict checks, audit evidence, and rules for changed orders.

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: What risks arise when the chart of accounts is redesigned during ERP implementation?
questions.preferred_answer: Risks include broken historical comparability, incorrect mappings, reporting gaps, integration failures, user confusion, and unreconciled opening balances. Use governance, mapping rules, mock conversions, parallel reporting, and sign-off by finance owners.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: How would you reconcile order-to-cash across CRM and ERP?
questions.preferred_answer: Agree authoritative systems and identifiers, then reconcile opportunity or order totals, customer, product, tax, fulfillment, invoice, payment, status, and timing. Exceptions should be explainable by documented process states rather than silently corrected.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 3. ERP Finance, Procure-to-Pay and Order-to-Cash
questions.question: A business requests direct journal posting by many operational users. How would you respond?
questions.preferred_answer: Challenge the control objective, volume, and alternatives such as controlled subledger transactions, templates, imports, or workflow. Limit direct journals to trained roles, enforce approvals and evidence, monitor sensitive accounts, and preserve segregation of duties.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is an item or product master?
questions.preferred_answer: The item master contains governed attributes used to buy, sell, plan, store, manufacture, price, and report a product or service. Shared definitions and ownership are essential because errors propagate across many processes.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is a bill of materials?
questions.preferred_answer: A bill of materials defines the components and quantities required to produce or assemble an item. Effective dates, alternatives, units of measure, scrap, and change control affect planning and costing.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is material requirements planning?
questions.preferred_answer: MRP calculates time-phased supply proposals from demand, inventory, lead times, lot-sizing rules, bills of materials, and planning parameters. Its output is only as reliable as the underlying master data and demand signals.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is available-to-promise?
questions.preferred_answer: Available-to-promise estimates whether and when demand can be fulfilled using supply, inventory, allocations, lead times, and business rules. It supports realistic customer commitments but depends on timely transactions and planning accuracy.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: Why are units of measure a major implementation concern?
questions.preferred_answer: Purchasing, stocking, production, and selling may use different units and conversions. Incorrect precision or conversion rules cause inventory, pricing, costing, tax, and fulfillment errors, so ownership and test coverage are required.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is safety stock?
questions.preferred_answer: Safety stock is buffer inventory intended to absorb demand or supply variability. It should be based on service targets and variability, reviewed periodically, and not used to hide poor data or process performance.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: How do lot and serial tracking differ?
questions.preferred_answer: Lot tracking groups units produced or received together, while serial tracking identifies individual units. The choice affects traceability, recalls, warranty, inventory operations, data volume, and scanning requirements.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What controls are important for inventory adjustments?
questions.preferred_answer: Restrict access, require reason codes and evidence, apply approval thresholds, count or verify high-risk items, preserve before-and-after quantities and value, and monitor recurring patterns by user, location, and item.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is cycle counting?
questions.preferred_answer: Cycle counting verifies selected inventory throughout the year instead of relying only on a full physical count. Count frequency should reflect value, movement, risk, and prior accuracy, with tolerances and root-cause follow-up.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: How does a routing differ from a bill of materials?
questions.preferred_answer: A bill of materials specifies what components are needed; a routing specifies operations, sequence, resources, and standard times. Together they support scheduling, capacity, costing, and production execution.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What is project accounting in an ERP?
questions.preferred_answer: Project accounting captures budgets, costs, commitments, time, revenue, billing, and profitability by project or work structure. It requires consistent links between operational transactions and financial dimensions.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: Why is worker or employee master data sensitive?
questions.preferred_answer: It may include identity, organizational, payroll, tax, bank, performance, and personal information. Access must follow role, purpose, geography, retention, and privacy requirements, with strong controls over interfaces and exports.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: How would you diagnose persistent negative inventory?
questions.preferred_answer: Examine transaction timing, backdated posting, integration delays, unit conversions, location rules, reservations, returns, and physical process. Correct the process and configuration rather than repeatedly posting balancing adjustments.

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: How would you design master data governance for a global product catalog?
questions.preferred_answer: Define global and local attributes, owners, approval workflow, naming and classification standards, duplicate checks, effective dates, quality metrics, downstream distribution, and change impact. Local variations should be controlled rather than copied into separate unmanaged masters.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: What should be considered when integrating payroll with finance?
questions.preferred_answer: Map earning, deduction, tax, benefit, liability, cost center, project, and legal entity dimensions; protect personal data; reconcile totals and headcount; manage reversals; and align posting and close calendars. Failures need secure rerun procedures.

source.title: Oracle - REST API for Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications

questions.category: 4. Supply Chain, Inventory, Manufacturing, Projects and Human Resources
questions.question: A manufacturer wants MRP to fix chronic late deliveries. What would you assess first?
questions.preferred_answer: Assess demand quality, lead times, capacity, yield, safety stock, supplier performance, transaction timeliness, BOM and routing accuracy, and planning discipline. MRP can expose and plan around constraints, but it cannot compensate for uncontrolled data and execution.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is the difference between a lead, account, contact, and opportunity?
questions.preferred_answer: A lead is an unqualified prospect record; an account represents an organization or customer entity; a contact represents a person; and an opportunity represents a potential revenue event. Exact models vary, but conversion and ownership rules must be clear.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is a sales pipeline stage?
questions.preferred_answer: A pipeline stage represents a defined step in the sales process with entry and exit criteria, expected actions, ownership, and probability or forecast treatment. Stages should reflect actual buyer and seller progress, not subjective optimism.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is a customer service case?
questions.preferred_answer: A case records a customer issue, request, complaint, or inquiry and tracks categorization, priority, ownership, communication, resolution, and service commitments. It should connect to the relevant customer, product, entitlement, and knowledge.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is a CRM activity?
questions.preferred_answer: An activity records an interaction or planned action such as a call, meeting, email, or task. Activities should support useful context and follow-up without creating excessive administrative burden or privacy risk.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How should lead qualification criteria be designed?
questions.preferred_answer: Define objective indicators of fit, need, authority, timing, engagement, and disqualifying conditions. The criteria should guide routing and follow-up, be measurable, and be reviewed against conversion outcomes.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is territory management?
questions.preferred_answer: Territory management assigns accounts, prospects, or opportunities based on geography, segment, product, industry, capacity, or other rules. It affects ownership, sharing, quotas, service, and reporting, so changes require controlled recalculation and communication.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How should opportunity probabilities be used?
questions.preferred_answer: Probabilities should follow consistent stage definitions or a documented predictive model. They support expected value and forecasting, but they should not replace judgment about timing, amount, risk, and data freshness.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is campaign attribution?
questions.preferred_answer: Campaign attribution assigns credit for customer engagement or revenue to marketing activities using defined rules or models. It requires consistent campaign membership, identity resolution, time windows, and transparency about limitations.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How do queues and routing support customer service?
questions.preferred_answer: Queues group work awaiting assignment; routing distributes it using priority, skill, capacity, language, channel, or entitlement. The design should prevent starvation, preserve ownership, and expose backlog and aging.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What is an SLA or entitlement in customer service?
questions.preferred_answer: It defines the service commitment a customer is eligible to receive, such as response and resolution targets, support hours, or covered products. Timers, pause conditions, escalations, and exceptions must match the contract and operating model.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: Why is a CRM knowledge base valuable?
questions.preferred_answer: A governed knowledge base improves consistency, self-service, resolution speed, and onboarding. Articles need ownership, review dates, searchability, access controls, usage feedback, and retirement processes.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What does omnichannel mean in CRM?
questions.preferred_answer: Omnichannel coordinates customer interactions across channels while preserving context, identity, routing, and consistent service. It is more than adding channels; it requires shared process and data across them.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How would you improve poor CRM adoption among sales users?
questions.preferred_answer: Observe the actual sales workflow, remove unnecessary fields and duplicate entry, improve mobile and integration support, clarify value, train managers, measure usage quality, and make the CRM the easiest path to complete real work. Avoid solving adoption only with mandates.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How would you design customer consent and communication preferences?
questions.preferred_answer: Capture purpose, channel, legal basis where applicable, source, timestamp, jurisdiction, expiry or withdrawal, and downstream enforcement. Make preferences easy to update and ensure integrations do not reintroduce prohibited contact.

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: What are key design concerns in configure-price-quote integration?
questions.preferred_answer: Product and price authority, eligibility, bundles, discounts, approvals, tax, currency, contract terms, versioning, order creation, and auditability must be aligned. Quote changes should not create silent inconsistencies with orders or invoices.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 5. CRM Sales, Marketing, Customer Service and Field Service
questions.question: How would you distinguish a service backlog problem from a routing problem?
questions.preferred_answer: Compare incoming volume, capacity, handle time, skill distribution, assignment delay, reopen rate, priority mix, and aging by queue. Routing can improve distribution, but sustained excess demand or poor resolution quality requires capacity and process action.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is master data management?
questions.preferred_answer: Master data management establishes governance, processes, and technology for consistent core entities such as customers, products, suppliers, and locations. It defines ownership, quality, identity, lifecycle, and distribution rather than only centralizing records.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is reference data?
questions.preferred_answer: Reference data is a controlled set of allowable values used to classify other data, such as countries, currencies, payment terms, statuses, or reason codes. Changes can affect rules, integrations, and reporting and therefore need governance.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is a golden record?
questions.preferred_answer: A golden record is the trusted representation of an entity created by matching and consolidating data according to governance and survivorship rules. It should retain source lineage and not hide unresolved conflicts.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What are common data quality dimensions?
questions.preferred_answer: Common dimensions include accuracy, completeness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, timeliness, and integrity. Each metric needs a defined rule, owner, threshold, and business impact.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is a data owner and how is that different from a data steward?
questions.preferred_answer: A data owner is accountable for policy, access, quality, and use of a data domain. A steward performs ongoing governance activities such as definitions, issue management, rule maintenance, and coordination; responsibilities may be distributed but must be explicit.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: How do matching rules and duplicate rules work together?
questions.preferred_answer: Matching rules determine whether records are similar enough to be potential duplicates; duplicate rules determine whether to allow, warn, block, or report the action. Thresholds should be tested against false positives and false negatives.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What are survivorship rules?
questions.preferred_answer: Survivorship rules decide which source value is retained when records conflict, using factors such as source authority, recency, completeness, verification, or manual stewardship. They should be transparent and reversible where possible.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: Why are external identifiers useful?
questions.preferred_answer: Stable external IDs link records across systems, support upsert and reconciliation, and reduce dependence on names or internal database keys. They need uniqueness, ownership, lifecycle, and collision controls.

source.title: Salesforce Developers - REST API Developer Guide

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: How should customer hierarchies be governed?
questions.preferred_answer: Define relationship types, effective dates, legal and commercial meaning, source authority, ownership, and reporting use. A single hierarchy may not serve billing, sales, risk, and service equally, so purpose-specific views may be needed.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is data lineage?
questions.preferred_answer: Data lineage shows where data originated, how it was transformed, where it moved, and which reports or processes depend on it. It supports impact analysis, troubleshooting, audit, and trust.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: How do validation rules improve data quality?
questions.preferred_answer: Validation rules prevent or flag values that violate defined conditions at entry or import. They should target meaningful errors, provide actionable messages, handle integrations, and avoid blocking legitimate exceptions without an approved path.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What is data reconciliation?
questions.preferred_answer: Reconciliation compares source and target counts, totals, keys, balances, statuses, and exceptions to prove completeness and correctness. It should use independent control totals and signed ownership rather than visual spot checks alone.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: How would you design duplicate prevention for a global customer database?
questions.preferred_answer: Use normalized fields, region-aware matching, tax or registration IDs where lawful, hierarchy and household logic, source priority, review queues, and monitoring. Test with representative languages and naming patterns before blocking records.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: How should an organization handle conflicting definitions of active customer?
questions.preferred_answer: Document each business purpose, appoint an accountable owner, define a canonical metric or explicitly named variants, specify timing and source data, and update reports and processes. Do not force one definition when regulatory, commercial, and service uses genuinely differ.

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: What controls are needed for bulk data correction?
questions.preferred_answer: Use approved scope, backup or export, test environment validation, peer review, least-privilege execution, change records, before-and-after evidence, reconciliation, and rollback. Protect automation from partial failure and unintended selection.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 6. Data Models, Master Data, Reference Data and Data Quality
questions.question: A migration has correct record counts but wrong parent-child relationships. What went wrong?
questions.preferred_answer: Counts prove volume, not relational integrity. Investigate source keys, mapping, load order, duplicate resolution, external IDs, failed references, and transformation rules; validate relationship samples and orphan counts before acceptance.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is metadata-driven configuration?
questions.preferred_answer: Metadata-driven configuration stores application behavior such as entities, fields, forms, rules, and workflows as managed definitions rather than hard-coded changes to the product core. It generally improves portability and upgrade support.

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is a low-code business application?
questions.preferred_answer: A low-code application uses visual designers, declarative logic, managed connectors, and reusable components to deliver business functionality with limited custom code. It still requires architecture, security, testing, lifecycle, and ownership.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is an approval workflow?
questions.preferred_answer: An approval workflow routes a transaction or request to authorized decision makers based on rules, thresholds, and conditions. It should define delegation, escalation, rejection, evidence, and behavior when data changes after approval.

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is a custom object or custom entity?
questions.preferred_answer: It is a platform-defined data structure created for a business concept not adequately represented by standard entities. Before creating one, confirm ownership, relationships, security, reporting, integration, and lifecycle requirements.

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: When is customization justified?
questions.preferred_answer: Customization is justified when a validated requirement cannot be met through process change, standard configuration, integration, or another governed capability and the business value exceeds lifecycle cost and risk. The decision should be documented and owned.

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What are extension points?
questions.preferred_answer: Extension points are supported mechanisms such as events, APIs, plugins, hooks, or add-ins that allow behavior to be added without modifying the product core. Supported points reduce upgrade risk compared with direct changes.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How would you govern business rules created by citizen developers?
questions.preferred_answer: Use environment strategy, data loss prevention, approved connectors, role-based access, naming, ownership, testing, solution packaging, monitoring, and retirement. Higher-risk applications should receive professional review and support planning.

source.title: Microsoft - Power Platform security and governance

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is the risk of putting too much logic in form scripts?
questions.preferred_answer: Form logic can be hard to reuse, test, secure, and execute consistently across imports, APIs, mobile, and background processes. Critical rules should be enforced at the appropriate server or data layer, with the user interface providing guidance.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How should approval workflow changes be tested?
questions.preferred_answer: Test every threshold, role, delegation, rejection, resubmission, timeout, escalation, data-change condition, and audit trail. Include unauthorized users, integration-created records, and failure recovery.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is solution packaging?
questions.preferred_answer: Solution packaging groups related metadata, components, dependencies, and versions so changes can be promoted across environments consistently. Packages should be source-controlled where supported and deployed through governed pipelines.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How do feature flags help business application releases?
questions.preferred_answer: Feature flags separate deployment from activation, enabling staged rollout, testing, and rapid disablement. They require ownership, default behavior, monitoring, security review, and cleanup to avoid permanent complexity.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: What is customization debt?
questions.preferred_answer: Customization debt is the accumulated cost and risk of bespoke behavior, duplicated logic, unsupported components, weak documentation, and deferred refactoring. It appears during upgrades, testing, support, security review, and skill turnover.

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How would you choose between workflow, plugin, integration, and robotic automation?
questions.preferred_answer: Choose based on transaction boundary, latency, reliability, data ownership, security, volume, error handling, observability, and product support. Prefer the simplest supported mechanism that preserves controls and can be operated safely.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How can low-code platforms create shadow IT risk?
questions.preferred_answer: Easy creation can produce unmanaged data stores, excessive permissions, fragile integrations, unowned apps, duplicated capability, and licensing exposure. Governance should enable safe delivery rather than simply prohibit development.

source.title: Microsoft - Power Platform security and governance

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: How would you review an upgrade-sensitive customization?
questions.preferred_answer: Identify product-core dependencies, deprecated APIs, unsupported database access, client assumptions, security context, performance, test coverage, and rollback. Replace direct modifications with supported extensions where feasible.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 7. Configuration, Customization, Low-Code and Extensibility
questions.question: A department asks for a quick low-code app that stores sensitive customer data. What do you require before approval?
questions.preferred_answer: Confirm business owner, data classification, lawful use, access model, retention, approved environment and connectors, audit, backup, support, testing, and integration with authoritative systems. Speed does not remove security and lifecycle obligations.

source.title: Microsoft - Power Platform security and governance

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is an API?
questions.preferred_answer: An application programming interface is a defined contract that allows software components to exchange requests, responses, events, or data. A usable enterprise API also needs authentication, authorization, versioning, error handling, limits, and operational ownership.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is middleware?
questions.preferred_answer: Middleware coordinates communication between applications through capabilities such as routing, transformation, orchestration, security, messaging, and monitoring. It can reduce point-to-point complexity but becomes critical shared infrastructure that must be governed.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How do synchronous and asynchronous integrations differ?
questions.preferred_answer: Synchronous integration waits for a response in the same interaction and suits immediate decisions. Asynchronous integration decouples systems through messages or events and improves resilience and scale, but requires state, retries, ordering, and reconciliation.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is a webhook?
questions.preferred_answer: A webhook is an HTTP callback sent when an event occurs. Consumers must authenticate the sender, handle duplicates and retries, validate payloads, respond quickly, and monitor missed events.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is idempotency and why does it matter?
questions.preferred_answer: An idempotent operation can be repeated without causing unintended additional effects. It prevents duplicate orders, payments, cases, or updates when clients retry after timeouts or partial failures.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How should integration retries be designed?
questions.preferred_answer: Retry only transient failures, use bounded exponential backoff and jitter, preserve correlation and idempotency keys, and route exhausted messages to a review or dead-letter path. Permanent validation errors need correction, not repeated load.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is a dead-letter queue?
questions.preferred_answer: A dead-letter queue holds messages that could not be processed after defined attempts. It supports investigation and controlled replay, but needs alerting, ownership, retention, security, and tools to avoid becoming a silent backlog.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How do REST and SOAP commonly differ?
questions.preferred_answer: REST commonly uses resource-oriented HTTP and JSON, while SOAP uses XML envelopes and formal service contracts with mature enterprise standards. The correct choice depends on platform capability, contract, security, transaction, and interoperability needs.

source.title: Oracle - REST API for Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How should API rate limits be handled?
questions.preferred_answer: Understand the quota and reset model, reduce unnecessary calls, use batching or caching, schedule bulk work, apply backoff, monitor consumption, and coordinate limits across integrations. Never treat repeated throttling as a random error.

source.title: Salesforce Developers - REST API Developer Guide

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is a canonical data model?
questions.preferred_answer: A canonical model is a shared representation used to reduce pairwise transformations between systems. It can simplify integration, but it should be scoped and governed because an overly universal model becomes slow and difficult to evolve.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What is schema versioning?
questions.preferred_answer: Schema versioning manages contract changes so producers and consumers can evolve without uncontrolled breakage. Favor backward-compatible additions, explicit deprecation, consumer testing, and observed usage before removal.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: What observability should an enterprise integration provide?
questions.preferred_answer: Capture correlation IDs, source and target, timestamps, status, latency, retries, payload metadata, error category, queue depth, and reconciliation totals while protecting sensitive content. Alerts should map to business impact and ownership.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How would you decide between real-time and batch integration?
questions.preferred_answer: Use business latency requirements, volume, transaction consistency, source capability, cost, recoverability, and user experience. Real-time adds operational complexity; batch may be safer when timely reconciliation is more important than immediate propagation.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How would you secure an integration service account?
questions.preferred_answer: Use a nonhuman identity, least privilege, strong credential or certificate management, short-lived tokens where possible, network and conditional controls, audit, rotation, usage monitoring, and a named owner. Do not share interactive user credentials.

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: How do you reconcile an event-driven integration when events arrive out of order?
questions.preferred_answer: Use event IDs, sequence or version data, timestamps with caution, idempotent upsert, state checks, buffering where required, and periodic source-to-target reconciliation. Business rules should define whether stale events are ignored or compensated.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 8. Integration, APIs, Middleware and Event-Driven Architecture
questions.question: An API integration creates duplicate sales orders after network timeouts. What is your response?
questions.preferred_answer: Stop or contain retries, identify duplicate scope, use idempotency keys or source transaction IDs, make creation safely repeatable, reconcile affected orders, and test timeout paths. Do not rely only on faster networks or manual deletion.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is authentication?
questions.preferred_answer: Authentication verifies the identity of a user, service, or device. It should use appropriate assurance such as MFA, federation, certificates, or managed identities before authorization decisions are made.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is authorization?
questions.preferred_answer: Authorization determines what an authenticated identity may do and which data it may access. In business applications it commonly combines roles, privileges, organizational scope, ownership, sharing, and field-level controls.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is role-based access control?
questions.preferred_answer: RBAC assigns permissions to roles aligned with job functions and assigns users to those roles. It improves consistency and reviewability, but roles need ownership, lifecycle management, and controls against excessive combinations.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is least privilege?
questions.preferred_answer: Least privilege gives identities only the access required for approved duties, for the shortest practical time and scope. It reduces accidental and malicious impact and should apply to users, administrators, integrations, and support staff.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is segregation of duties?
questions.preferred_answer: Segregation of duties prevents one person from controlling incompatible steps of a sensitive process, such as creating a supplier and releasing payment. Conflicts should be prevented where possible or mitigated through approved review and monitoring.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How do business roles and data roles differ?
questions.preferred_answer: A business or job role defines functional privileges; a data role or security context restricts where those privileges apply, such as legal entity, business unit, territory, or department. Both are needed to avoid broad access.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is field-level security?
questions.preferred_answer: Field-level security controls whether a user can view or change specific attributes even when the record itself is accessible. It is useful for sensitive fields but must also be enforced through APIs, reports, exports, and integrations.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How does record sharing differ from object permission?
questions.preferred_answer: Object permission allows actions on a type of record; record sharing determines which specific records are visible or editable. A user may have read permission on accounts but see only assigned or shared accounts.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What is a privileged access review?
questions.preferred_answer: It is a periodic and event-driven review of administrative, implementation, support, and emergency access to confirm need, scope, ownership, and activity. Unused or unjustified privileges should be removed promptly.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What should an audit trail record?
questions.preferred_answer: Record who performed an action, what changed, when, from where or through which interface, the before-and-after value where appropriate, and relevant context. Logs need protection, retention, searchable access, and monitoring.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How should break-glass access be controlled?
questions.preferred_answer: Use separate emergency identities, strong authentication, vaulting, time limits, approval or documented emergency use, real-time alerting, complete logging, and mandatory post-use review. It must not become routine administrator access.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: What security concerns apply to data exports?
questions.preferred_answer: Exports can bypass normal screen controls and create unmanaged copies. Restrict export privileges, apply field security, classify and protect files, log usage, enforce retention, and review bulk or unusual activity.

source.title: Microsoft - Power Platform security and governance

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How would you design access for external partners using a CRM portal?
questions.preferred_answer: Separate identities, least-privilege roles, record-level sharing, strong authentication, data minimization, tenant or account boundaries, secure registration, monitoring, and tested revocation. Never rely only on hidden navigation.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How should segregation-of-duties conflicts be handled when staffing is limited?
questions.preferred_answer: Document the conflict and business necessity, minimize access, require independent approval or review, monitor sensitive transactions, rotate duties where possible, and set an expiry. A mitigation is an owned control, not a permanent exception note.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: How would you investigate suspected unauthorized access to customer records?
questions.preferred_answer: Preserve audit and identity evidence, scope accounts and records, suspend or restrict access if necessary, review roles, sharing, sessions, exports, and integrations, follow incident and privacy procedures, and remediate the root cause without altering evidence.

questions.category: 9. Identity, Security, Roles, Segregation of Duties, Privacy and Audit
questions.question: A consultant requests a broad implementation role in production for convenience. What would you do?
questions.preferred_answer: Require task-specific, time-bound access, separate setup from operational data where possible, obtain accountable approval, monitor activity, and remove access after use. Convenience does not justify unrestricted implementation privileges.

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What are the main stages of data migration?
questions.preferred_answer: Typical stages are scope and inventory, profiling, cleansing, mapping, transformation, mock extraction and load, validation, cutover, reconciliation, and post-load support. Governance and ownership span every stage.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is a migration mapping document?
questions.preferred_answer: It defines how source objects and fields map to targets, including transformations, defaults, reference lookups, ownership, exclusions, validation, and error handling. It should be versioned and traceable to tests.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is a mock migration?
questions.preferred_answer: A mock migration runs the planned extraction, transformation, load, validation, and timing in a nonproduction environment. Repeated mocks expose data, tooling, dependency, performance, and cutover problems before go-live.

source.title: SAP Help - The S/4HANA migration process

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is cutover?
questions.preferred_answer: Cutover is the coordinated transition from old processes and systems to the new solution, including freezes, final data loads, configuration, access, integration switch, validation, communication, and contingency decisions.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How do historical, open, and master data differ in migration planning?
questions.preferred_answer: Master data enables operations; open transactions must continue correctly in the target; historical closed transactions may be migrated, summarized, archived, or accessed through a legacy solution. The choice depends on legal, reporting, service, cost, and performance needs.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: Why are data profiling and cleansing performed before mapping is finalized?
questions.preferred_answer: Profiling reveals actual formats, nulls, duplicates, invalid values, volumes, and relationships. This evidence changes mapping and cleansing rules and prevents designs based only on outdated field descriptions.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How should parent-child records be loaded?
questions.preferred_answer: Preserve stable source identifiers, load parents or referenced masters first, capture target IDs where needed, then load children with validated relationships. Measure orphans and failed references explicitly.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is delta migration?
questions.preferred_answer: Delta migration transfers changes made after an earlier extraction or mock load. It requires a reliable change boundary, timestamps or logs, deletion handling, idempotency, and reconciliation so no record is missed or duplicated.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What is a data freeze and why is it used?
questions.preferred_answer: A data freeze limits changes during final migration so source and target can be reconciled. The freeze should be as short and targeted as possible, with approved emergency changes captured for later delta processing.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How do you validate a migrated financial balance?
questions.preferred_answer: Reconcile controlled totals by entity, account, currency, period, and subledger; compare counts and exception reports; sample source documents; and obtain finance ownership sign-off. Conversion journals must be separately identifiable.

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What should happen to failed migration records?
questions.preferred_answer: Classify the error, preserve the source and error detail, correct data or rules under change control, rerun idempotently, and update reconciliation. Do not silently exclude failed records or manually recreate them without traceability.

source.title: SAP Help - The S/4HANA migration process

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How should data ownership be assigned during migration?
questions.preferred_answer: Business owners approve scope, definitions, cleansing, and acceptance; technical teams implement extraction and load. Stewards manage detailed issues. Every critical object and reconciliation should have named accountability.

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How would you plan migration of customer records from multiple CRMs?
questions.preferred_answer: Define identity and hierarchy rules, source authority, duplicates, consent, ownership, activities, attachments, external IDs, and source retention. Run staged matching and stewardship before loading the target and reconcile by source and business unit.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: What makes a migration rollback plan credible?
questions.preferred_answer: It defines the decision authority and deadline, how business transactions are stopped or reversed, restoration of systems and integrations, handling of data created after cutover, user communication, and rehearsed technical steps. Some transformations may require forward recovery rather than simple rollback.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: How would you determine whether to migrate attachments and activity history?
questions.preferred_answer: Evaluate legal retention, operational need, search, privacy, volume, cost, performance, metadata quality, and alternative archival access. Migrate only what users and obligations need, with links and permissions preserved.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 10. Data Migration, Cutover and Reconciliation
questions.question: The final migration completes within the window, but reconciliation has unexplained differences. Do you go live?
questions.preferred_answer: Do not accept unexplained material differences. Assess business and control impact, isolate whether discrepancies are timing or defects, obtain accountable decision-making, correct or invoke contingency, and preserve evidence. Schedule success alone is not acceptance.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What is system integration testing?
questions.preferred_answer: SIT validates that connected components, applications, interfaces, jobs, and end-to-end flows work together with correct data and error handling. It is broader than testing each configuration in isolation.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What is user acceptance testing?
questions.preferred_answer: UAT is business-led validation that the solution supports agreed processes, controls, roles, and outcomes using representative scenarios and data. It is not a substitute for technical testing.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What is regression testing?
questions.preferred_answer: Regression testing confirms that previously working capability still works after a change. Prioritize critical end-to-end processes, integrations, controls, and historically fragile areas rather than rerunning only the changed screen.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: Why test security roles?
questions.preferred_answer: Role testing confirms that users can complete authorized work and cannot access prohibited functions or data. Test positive and negative access through UI, reports, exports, APIs, and delegated administration.

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What should an ERP end-to-end test case contain?
questions.preferred_answer: Include business objective, preconditions, roles, master data, steps across systems, expected postings and statuses, controls, integrations, reports, exceptions, and evidence. It should mirror a complete business outcome rather than one module transaction.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How do UAT and training differ?
questions.preferred_answer: UAT verifies that the solution meets acceptance criteria; training builds user capability. UAT participants may learn during execution, but scripted pass results should not depend on trainers correcting the system or completing steps for users.

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What test data is needed for a CRM implementation?
questions.preferred_answer: Use representative customers, prospects, hierarchies, products, territories, consent states, opportunities, cases, integrations, duplicates, and exceptions. Protect personal data and ensure tests cover different roles and regions.

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How should migration testing be structured?
questions.preferred_answer: Test extraction, transformation, load, relationships, permissions, reconciliation, performance, rerun, failure recovery, and business usability over repeated mocks. Validate both correct records and expected rejects.

source.title: Salesforce Help - Data migration best practices

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What are test entry and exit criteria?
questions.preferred_answer: Entry criteria define readiness such as stable build, data, environment, and resolved blockers. Exit criteria define acceptable coverage, pass rate, defect position, performance, reconciliation, and approvals; they make decisions explicit.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How should defects be triaged?
questions.preferred_answer: Classify business impact, severity, scope, reproducibility, control and data risk, workaround, ownership, and release effect. Priority is a decision about when to act, not simply another name for severity.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: Where is test automation most valuable in business applications?
questions.preferred_answer: Automate stable, repeatable, high-value regression such as APIs, calculations, integrations, role checks, and critical transaction paths. Avoid brittle UI automation where configuration changes frequently unless the risk justifies maintenance.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: What should performance testing cover in ERP or CRM?
questions.preferred_answer: Test realistic concurrency, transaction mix, data volumes, reports, imports, batch jobs, integrations, peak periods, and degraded dependencies. Measure user response, throughput, queues, resource limits, and recovery.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How would you test an approval workflow with complex thresholds?
questions.preferred_answer: Use boundary values, all role combinations, delegation, escalation, rejection, resubmission, changed amounts, split transactions, unavailable approvers, integration-created records, and unauthorized attempts. Verify audit evidence and notifications.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How do you prevent UAT from becoming informal demonstration?
questions.preferred_answer: Provide traceable scenarios and expected results, independent business execution, controlled data, defect capture, evidence, coverage reporting, and accountable sign-off. Demonstrations can prepare users but should not be counted as acceptance.

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: How would you test a multi-system order-to-cash process?
questions.preferred_answer: Cover customer and product sync, pricing, credit, order creation, fulfillment, tax, invoice, payment, status updates, errors, retries, duplicates, security, and financial reconciliation. Include partial, cancelled, returned, and backordered paths.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 11. Testing, UAT, Regression and Quality Assurance
questions.question: A critical defect is found during go-live readiness but has a manual workaround. How do you decide?
questions.preferred_answer: Assess business volume, error and control risk, user capability, data impact, monitoring, duration, ownership, and rollback. A workaround must be documented, tested, approved, and time-bounded; schedule pressure alone is not acceptance.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is implementation governance?
questions.preferred_answer: Implementation governance defines decision rights, accountability, controls, escalation, scope, quality gates, and reporting for the program. It ensures business and technical decisions are made by the appropriate owners.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is a RACI matrix?
questions.preferred_answer: RACI identifies who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for activities and decisions. Each important outcome should have one clear accountable owner.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is change management in a business application program?
questions.preferred_answer: Change management prepares people and the operating model to adopt new processes, roles, controls, data, and technology. It includes stakeholder engagement, impact analysis, communication, training, readiness, reinforcement, and feedback.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is hypercare?
