questions.preferred_answer: Hypercare is a time-bound period of heightened monitoring and support after go-live. It uses clear command, triage, staffing, metrics, knowledge transfer, and exit criteria before transition to steady-state support.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What are typical phases of a business application implementation?
questions.preferred_answer: Common phases include strategy and value definition, initiation and design, build and configuration, testing and preparation, deployment, and operation. Iterative delivery may repeat these phases for capabilities or releases.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is the role of an executive sponsor?
questions.preferred_answer: The sponsor owns the business case, resolves cross-functional barriers, secures resources, reinforces process decisions, and holds leaders accountable for adoption and benefits. Sponsorship cannot be delegated entirely to the project manager.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How does a process owner differ from a project manager?
questions.preferred_answer: The process owner is accountable for the ongoing business process, controls, and outcomes. The project manager coordinates delivery scope, schedule, resources, risks, and dependencies; both roles collaborate but have different accountability.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How should fit-to-standard workshops be governed?
questions.preferred_answer: Use defined process scope, decision owners, standard demonstrations, requirement and gap logs, time-boxed decisions, and escalation. Participants should distinguish legal or value-creating needs from preferences based on the legacy system.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is a RAID log?
questions.preferred_answer: A RAID log tracks Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies with owners, dates, impact, action, and status. It should support decisions and escalation rather than become a passive list.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How should scope changes be controlled?
questions.preferred_answer: Record the requested change, rationale, value, effort, risk, architecture, testing, training, timeline, and benefit impact. An authorized forum decides whether to approve, defer, reject, or exchange scope.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What is a super-user network?
questions.preferred_answer: Super users are trained business representatives who support design validation, testing, training, adoption, and local issue resolution. They need recognized capacity, clear responsibilities, and a path to the product and support teams.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How should adoption be measured?
questions.preferred_answer: Measure meaningful use and process outcomes, such as completion in the system, data quality, active use by role, workaround reduction, cycle time, error rate, and user confidence. Login counts alone are weak evidence.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How would you organize a global template with local legal requirements?
questions.preferred_answer: Define a governed global process and data core, document permitted localization, assign global and local decision rights, use reusable configuration patterns, and prevent local changes from undermining shared controls and reporting.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: What are the risks of a big-bang implementation?
questions.preferred_answer: A big bang concentrates migration, process, integration, training, and operational risk into one event. It can reduce prolonged coexistence but requires stronger rehearsal, readiness evidence, contingency, and support capacity.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: How should implementation partners be governed?
questions.preferred_answer: Define deliverables, quality standards, knowledge transfer, architecture and security obligations, evidence, access controls, issue escalation, acceptance criteria, and commercial incentives. Internal owners must retain decisions and capability.

questions.category: 12. Implementation Methods, Governance, Change and Adoption
questions.question: A sponsor insists on the original go-live date despite incomplete UAT and training. How would you respond?
questions.preferred_answer: Present evidence of uncovered process, control, adoption, and operational risk; propose recovery options and decision thresholds; document accountable risk acceptance; and protect mandatory controls. The decision should be transparent, not hidden in optimistic status reporting.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is a KPI?
questions.preferred_answer: A key performance indicator is a measurable value linked to an important objective and decision. It needs a precise definition, owner, source, frequency, target, and action when performance changes.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How does an operational report differ from an analytical report?
questions.preferred_answer: Operational reports support current transactions and exceptions, often with detailed and timely data. Analytical reports aggregate and model data for trends, comparison, forecasting, and decision-making.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is a dashboard?
questions.preferred_answer: A dashboard presents selected measures, trends, and exceptions for a defined audience and decision process. Good dashboards provide context and action rather than displaying every available metric.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is a semantic model?
questions.preferred_answer: A semantic model provides governed business concepts, relationships, measures, hierarchies, and security over data. It reduces inconsistent calculations and separates business meaning from physical source structures.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: Why must KPI definitions be governed?
questions.preferred_answer: Small differences in filters, timing, currency, status, or hierarchy can create conflicting results. Governance records the formula, data source, owner, version, exclusions, and approved use.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is data latency?
questions.preferred_answer: Data latency is the delay between a business event and its availability in a report or downstream system. The acceptable latency depends on the decision and should be visible to users.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How should row-level security be applied in reporting?
questions.preferred_answer: Apply user, role, geography, legal entity, territory, or ownership rules consistently in the semantic and source layers. Test exports, subscriptions, shared links, and service accounts, not only the interactive dashboard.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is drill-down and when is it useful?
questions.preferred_answer: Drill-down lets users move from summary to contributing detail along governed hierarchies. It supports explanation and action, but access controls and reconciled definitions must remain consistent.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How would you reconcile a dashboard total with ERP financial reports?
questions.preferred_answer: Confirm source, cutoff, currency, entity, account mapping, status, eliminations, refresh timing, and calculation logic. Use controlled totals and document expected timing differences instead of manually adjusting the dashboard.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is self-service BI governance?
questions.preferred_answer: It enables users to explore and create reports within certified data, security, naming, lifecycle, and support guardrails. Certification and ownership help distinguish trusted content from personal analysis.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How can calculated fields create reporting risk?
questions.preferred_answer: Logic may be duplicated, inconsistent, poorly documented, or evaluated differently across tools and times. Critical measures should be centralized, tested, versioned, and reconciled.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What affects report performance in a business application?
questions.preferred_answer: Data volume, joins, calculated logic, filters, indexes, security evaluation, refresh design, API limits, concurrency, and poorly scoped queries all matter. Performance tuning must preserve correctness and access control.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How would you design an executive dashboard for order-to-cash?
questions.preferred_answer: Link measures to decisions: order intake, backlog, fulfillment, billing, overdue receivables, cycle time, exceptions, and forecast. Show definitions, targets, trends, segmentation, data freshness, and drill paths to accountable action.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: How should forecast accuracy be evaluated?
questions.preferred_answer: Compare forecast snapshots with actual outcomes by period, segment, owner, and horizon; separate amount and timing error; and track bias. Avoid judging only the final forecast because late changes hide process quality.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: What is the risk of embedding analytics directly in transactional screens?
questions.preferred_answer: Embedded insight can improve decisions, but stale data, unclear definitions, excessive queries, security leakage, and cognitive overload can harm users. Use purpose-specific measures with visible freshness and tested performance.

questions.category: 13. Reporting, Analytics, KPIs and Embedded BI
questions.question: Two departments publish different customer-retention rates. How would you resolve it?
questions.preferred_answer: Trace definitions, cohorts, time windows, cancellations, renewals, source systems, and refresh timing. Agree a governed metric or clearly name valid variants, assign ownership, and update downstream reports and decisions.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: Why use separate development, test, and production environments?
questions.preferred_answer: Environment separation reduces the risk of untested changes affecting live operations and data. Each environment needs controlled purpose, access, configuration, data handling, and promotion rules.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What is application lifecycle management?
questions.preferred_answer: ALM governs requirements, design, build, versioning, testing, deployment, operation, and retirement of applications and configuration. It applies to low-code and packaged-business changes as well as custom code.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What is a deployment pipeline?
questions.preferred_answer: A deployment pipeline promotes versioned changes through stages with automated or controlled validation, approvals, and evidence. It aims to make releases repeatable and reduce manual variation.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: Why use source control for business application changes?
questions.preferred_answer: Source control preserves history, review, branching, traceability, and recovery for code and exportable metadata. It reduces dependence on a single environment or administrator.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What should be included in a release package?
questions.preferred_answer: Include versioned solution components, dependencies, configuration data, scripts, migration steps, security changes, test results, release notes, deployment order, validation, rollback, and support instructions.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How do managed and unmanaged solution concepts differ?
questions.preferred_answer: Managed packages are intended for controlled downstream deployment and protect ownership and upgrade behavior; unmanaged components are typically used during development and can be edited directly. Exact behavior is platform-specific, so teams must follow vendor lifecycle guidance.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How should configuration data move across environments?
questions.preferred_answer: Identify what is metadata versus business data, use supported export or migration tools, version-controlled reference sets, and environment-specific parameters. Avoid manual re-entry without reconciliation and evidence.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What is a smoke test after deployment?
questions.preferred_answer: A smoke test quickly checks that the application starts and critical paths, integrations, roles, jobs, and monitoring are functional. It is a release gate, not a replacement for regression testing.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What makes a rollback plan effective?
questions.preferred_answer: It defines trigger, decision authority, backups or previous package, database or data implications, integration state, user communication, validation, and time window. It must be tested for the actual release mechanism.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How should secrets be handled in deployment?
questions.preferred_answer: Keep secrets outside source packages, use managed vaults or secure platform connections, restrict access, rotate credentials, separate environments, and prevent logs from exposing values. Deployment automation should reference secret identifiers.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What is dependency management in packaged applications?
questions.preferred_answer: It tracks components, APIs, reference data, extensions, integrations, and versions required by a change. Missing or incompatible dependencies are a common cause of deployment and rollback failure.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How should hotfixes be controlled?
questions.preferred_answer: Use an expedited but documented path with impact assessment, targeted testing, approval, versioning, production validation, and merge-back to the main line. Emergency does not mean untraceable.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How would you manage a vendor deprecation that affects several integrations?
questions.preferred_answer: Inventory consumers, assess impact and deadlines, design replacement contracts, prioritize and fund changes, test in stages, monitor usage, communicate with owners, and remove old paths before vendor shutdown.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: What are the risks of manually editing production configuration?
questions.preferred_answer: Changes may be unreviewed, unreproducible, untested, overwritten, and absent from lower environments. Restrict emergency edits, capture exact changes, validate immediately, and back-port them into the governed source and pipeline.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: How would you design release governance for a shared global CRM?
questions.preferred_answer: Use a common roadmap, intake and architecture review, environment and branching strategy, regression suite, regional change windows, data and security review, release communications, and emergency path. Local changes must not bypass global ownership.

questions.category: 14. Application Lifecycle, Environments, Releases and DevOps
questions.question: A deployment succeeds technically but users see missing fields and wrong permissions. What do you investigate?
questions.preferred_answer: Check component inclusion, security role and field permission migration, dependency and layer precedence, environment-specific configuration, cache, license, and deployment logs. Compare the intended package with production and validate by representative roles.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What is application support for ERP and CRM?
questions.preferred_answer: Application support restores service, fulfills requests, maintains data and configuration, solves recurring problems, and enables safe change. It requires functional, technical, data, integration, and vendor coordination.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How does an incident differ from a service request?
questions.preferred_answer: An incident is an unplanned interruption or reduction in service; a service request is a predefined user request such as access, information, or a standard change. Classification affects priority, workflow, and reporting.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What is a batch job?
questions.preferred_answer: A batch job processes scheduled or queued work such as posting, billing, synchronization, reporting, or data maintenance. It needs dependency, duration, restart, alerting, and business-completion controls.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: Why is a knowledge base important for support?
questions.preferred_answer: It provides validated procedures, known errors, business context, and escalation guidance, improving consistency and reducing resolution time. Articles need ownership, evidence, review dates, and feedback.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How should ERP incidents be prioritized?
questions.preferred_answer: Use business impact, urgency, transaction volume, financial or control risk, user scope, deadlines, workaround, and data integrity. A single user can still be critical if the blocked function is unique or time-sensitive.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What should monitoring cover for business applications?
questions.preferred_answer: Monitor availability, user experience, integrations, queues, batch jobs, API limits, storage, errors, security events, performance, and business completion such as orders posted or invoices generated.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How would you investigate a failed overnight posting job?
questions.preferred_answer: Confirm scope and business deadline, review job and dependency logs, input data, locks, capacity, credentials, configuration, and prior changes. Restore safely, reconcile partial processing, communicate impact, and prevent recurrence.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What is a known error?
questions.preferred_answer: A known error is a problem with a documented cause or workaround that support can apply consistently while a permanent fix is planned. It should not become an excuse to leave high-risk defects unaddressed.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How should data-fix requests be handled?
questions.preferred_answer: Treat them as controlled changes: validate business authorization, scope, root cause, affected records, backup, test, peer review, execution identity, reconciliation, and audit evidence. Prefer correcting the process that created the bad data.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What operational risks arise near month-end or quarter-end?
questions.preferred_answer: Transaction volume, close dependencies, batch contention, integration delays, strict cutoffs, limited change windows, and senior reporting pressure increase impact. Use freeze rules, readiness checks, capacity monitoring, and command paths.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How should a vendor support case be raised?
questions.preferred_answer: Provide product and version, environment, business impact, severity rationale, timestamps, reproducible steps, logs, correlation IDs, recent changes, troubleshooting performed, and secure evidence. Maintain internal ownership rather than waiting passively.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What is root cause analysis in application operations?
questions.preferred_answer: RCA identifies the technical, process, data, control, and organizational conditions that allowed an issue, then assigns corrective actions and measures effectiveness. It should avoid blame and superficial causes such as user error alone.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How would you diagnose a CRM that becomes slow only for sales managers?
questions.preferred_answer: Compare role permissions, sharing calculations, dashboards, list views, data volume, plugins, browser traces, and territory hierarchy. Test representative users and isolate whether the delay is query, security evaluation, customization, or client behavior.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: How do you manage application capacity in SaaS?
questions.preferred_answer: Track storage, API quotas, job concurrency, license use, integration throughput, report load, and growth trends. Optimize behavior, archive responsibly, and plan entitlement changes before service limits affect operations.

source.title: Microsoft - Prepare a Dynamics 365 production environment to go live

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: What should a business application disaster recovery plan address?
questions.preferred_answer: Define critical processes, recovery time and point objectives, vendor capabilities, identity, integrations, data exports, manual workarounds, communication, testing, and responsibilities. SaaS availability does not eliminate customer continuity planning.

questions.category: 15. Operations, Support, Performance, Reliability and Vendor Management
questions.question: An integration queue is growing but no errors are visible. What would you do?
questions.preferred_answer: Check consumer throughput, throttling, locks, payload size, downstream latency, stuck messages, capacity, and monitoring gaps. Protect business deadlines, scale or drain safely, reconcile sequence, and add alerting on queue age and growth.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is SAP S/4HANA?
questions.preferred_answer: SAP S/4HANA is SAP's enterprise application suite built around an integrated ERP data and process model. Roles may focus on functional configuration, development, data, integration, security, analytics, or operations.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA Cloud documentation

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is the business partner concept in SAP S/4HANA?
questions.preferred_answer: Business Partner provides a central entity for persons and organizations with roles such as customer or supplier. Migration and integration must preserve role-specific data, relationships, identifiers, and governance.

source.title: SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA data migration

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What does the SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit do?
questions.preferred_answer: It supports initial migration using defined migration objects, mappings, simulation, transfer, and monitoring. It is designed for migration, not continuous system-to-system synchronization.

source.title: SAP Help - The S/4HANA migration process

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is Oracle Functional Setup Manager?
questions.preferred_answer: Functional Setup Manager organizes implementation tasks and setup data for Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications and supports moving verified setup between environments. Access must be assigned carefully to implementation users.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: How are roles and data access combined in Oracle Fusion Applications?
questions.preferred_answer: Oracle uses role-based access with job, abstract, duty, and data roles or security contexts. Functional privilege and the organizational data scope must both be assigned and reviewed.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is Microsoft Dataverse?
questions.preferred_answer: Dataverse is the managed data platform underlying many Dynamics 365 and Power Platform applications, providing tables, relationships, security, business logic, APIs, and solution lifecycle capabilities.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: How do Dynamics 365 security roles work?
questions.preferred_answer: Security roles grant privileges on tables and functions, while business units, teams, ownership, hierarchy, and field security shape record and field access. Role design should reflect job and data scope.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is a Power Platform solution?
questions.preferred_answer: A solution packages application components and dependencies for lifecycle management across environments. Teams should distinguish development and downstream packaging models and automate validation where possible.

source.title: Microsoft - Application lifecycle management with Power Platform

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What is the Salesforce object model?
questions.preferred_answer: Salesforce stores business data in standard and custom objects with fields and relationships. Good design uses standard capability where appropriate and governs ownership, access, automation, integration, and reporting.

source.title: Salesforce Developers - REST API Developer Guide

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What shapes record access in Salesforce?
questions.preferred_answer: Object permissions, field-level security, organization-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, territories, and manual or programmatic sharing combine to determine access. Test at scale because sharing design affects performance.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: How does Salesforce duplicate management support data quality?
questions.preferred_answer: Matching rules identify potential duplicates; duplicate rules decide whether to warn, block, or report them. Administrators should tune rules with data analysis and monitor false positives, false negatives, and user behavior.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What must be considered when integrating with Salesforce APIs?
questions.preferred_answer: Choose the appropriate API and pattern, use OAuth and least-privilege identities, respect limits, handle pagination and retries, preserve IDs, and monitor errors and consumption. Bulk and event use cases often need different interfaces.

source.title: Salesforce Architects - Integration patterns and practices

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: How do Odoo access rights and record rules differ?
questions.preferred_answer: Access rights allow create, read, update, or delete operations on a model; record rules restrict which records are accessible. Both must be tested, and administrator changes require strong control.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What should be checked before importing data into Odoo?
questions.preferred_answer: Validate identifiers, required fields, relational references, formats, duplicates, access, and a rollback or backup approach. Test a sample, review errors, and reconcile the final import.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: How would you choose among SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce, and Odoo for a business capability?
questions.preferred_answer: Start with process and industry fit, global and local requirements, data and integration architecture, security, extensibility, reporting, ecosystem skills, operating model, roadmap, total cost, and migration risk. Avoid selecting from brand familiarity alone.

questions.category: 16. Platform Specialization: SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Salesforce and Odoo
questions.question: What skills transfer across ERP and CRM platforms?
questions.preferred_answer: Business process analysis, data modeling, integration, security, migration, testing, reporting, change management, support, and lifecycle governance transfer well. Platform-specific configuration matters, but durable professionals can explain the underlying business and control principles.

labs.title: Map an end-to-end order-to-cash process

labs.title: Build a procure-to-pay approval matrix

labs.title: Design a CRM sales pipeline
labs.objective: Define lead qualification, opportunity stages, entry and exit criteria, probabilities, ownership, mandatory data, stale-record rules, and forecast treatment.

labs.title: Configure a customer-service case model
labs.objective: Design case categories, priority, queues, routing, SLA timers, escalation, knowledge use, closure codes, and reopen behavior.

labs.title: Create an ERP and CRM capability map
